title: A Woman’s Victory
paragraphs: The little one was moving in the direction of his mother
After having run, played in the water and blown bubbles of foam. The anklets he wore and his child’s patter made wonderful music.
Even as he was nearing his mother, The other woman in his father’s life stopped him to embrace and kiss him. Thinking that her son would reject the gestures and come to her, The mother waited along.

Seeing that he didn’t, She became angry and exclaimed, “The sprout will follow the seed.” He my man keeps saying, “You’re the elder sister While the other women in my life are your younger sisters. You’re the genuine pearl while the others are the fake ones.” But he goes after the other pearls.

She thought that if she remained silent not protesting, She might end up losing her relationship with her son as well. Just at this juncture, The son decked in ornaments came calling her ‘O mother!’. Her anger raging like a volcano subdued cool as snowfall. Spotting her husband she exclaimed, “Oh, here you are! Hereafter the boy alone would be the ray of hope dissipating my darkness; Today I start for my mother’s house along with him. Some men do exist, like the spots on the face of the moon, But you are a moon all in spots!
Intiraṉ himself should take a lesson or two from you in the art of winning women.
So long I exercised restraint with the fond hope of reforming you. You cannot bridle your habit of making merry every day.
My son who looks like the full moon is enough to provide me solace. You spoiled the family with a mind perverse, Your blotted life would teach you a fitting lesson before long.”
Bursting out thus, That speaking portrait was about to exit from the house Along with the soothing breeze on her lap.

The husband cried out in pain within, With his legs trembling As if he were stabbed by a thousand spears and swords in the chest. “Let the bygones be bygones! You might leave me immediately if it were to happen again. I don’t fancy a life without you, my singing bird! Like the singing birds let us live without any worry. Let’s lead an impeccable life which nobody can fault. I will ever remain faithful to you hereafter.” Coming around, he fell at her feet. “It is not enough if the people here stand witness. Let your former concubines also see this scene”, she said.

> As the hero’s concubine cuddles her son up in love > And lets him after play with him; > > As the hero approaches her unknown from behind > When she is absorbed in play with her son > And nestles up against her > In an act of virtuous conduct > And seeks to resolve her sulking; > > As she turns thereon to her son, > The source of unending joy that he is, > And holds him to reproach > Finding the adage ‘like father like son’ true; > > As she abides in the virtue of conjugal love > When she does not go dispirited > At the unkindly act of debauchery of the hero, > And takes the word of conciliation of the men of note; > > As she reveals her lofty trait of a wedded wife > When she tells him at his face > ‘It would look instructive (dishonourable?) > Were my younger sisters (the hero’s concubines) to see it’, > With the hero prostrating before her > And soliciting her pardon for his act of debauchery; > > ....
